items.name: React Native

license.scope: MIT for the upstream code; check bundled third-party notices.

items.summary: Framework for building native iOS and Android apps with React and JavaScript/TypeScript.
items.useWhen: Use instead of maintaining separate Swift and Kotlin codebases when a team already works in React. Start from Expo unless you need a bare native setup.
cautions: Native module compatibility varies across New Architecture versions; check each dependency.
Upgrades between minor versions can require native project changes.
install: Install with the project's package manager and commit the lockfile; pin the reviewed version.

items.name: Expo

license.scope: MIT for the upstream code; check bundled third-party notices.

items.summary: React Native framework and SDK with managed native modules, config plugins and build tooling.
items.useWhen: Use instead of hand-configuring Xcode/Gradle projects and writing common native modules (camera, notifications, file system) for a React Native app.
cautions: EAS Build/Submit/Update are paid hosted services beyond the free tier; the SDK itself is MIT.
Keep all expo-* packages on the SDK version the project targets.
install: Create with `npx create-expo-app@latest` and use `npx expo install` so native packages match the SDK.

items.name: Expo Router

license.scope: MIT for the upstream code; check bundled third-party notices.

items.summary: File-based router for Expo and React Native apps built on React Navigation, with deep linking.
items.useWhen: Use instead of hand-writing navigator trees and deep-link URL mapping in an Expo app.
cautions: Version is tied to the Expo SDK; install with `npx expo install`.
Typed routes and web output depend on the configured bundler.
install: Install with the project's package manager and commit the lockfile; pin the reviewed version.

items.name: React Navigation

license.scope: MIT for the upstream code; check bundled third-party notices.

items.summary: Stack, tab and drawer navigation library for React Native apps.
items.useWhen: Use instead of hand-building screen stacks, tab bars, back handling and navigation state persistence in React Native.
cautions: Requires peer native packages (screens, safe-area-context); match their versions.
Major versions change the API; follow the upgrade guide.
install: Install with the project's package manager and commit the lockfile; pin the reviewed version.

items.name: NativeWind

license.scope: MIT for the upstream code; check bundled third-party notices.

items.summary: Tailwind CSS utility classes for React Native components.
items.useWhen: Use instead of hand-writing StyleSheet objects and responsive/dark-mode style logic when the team already uses Tailwind tokens.
cautions: Pin the NativeWind and Tailwind CSS versions together; supported Tailwind majors differ by release.
Requires Babel/Metro configuration.

sources.title: Also listed in Awesome UI Resources

install: Install with the project's package manager and commit the lockfile; pin the reviewed version.

items.name: Tamagui

license.scope: MIT for the upstream code; check bundled third-party notices.

items.summary: Universal UI kit and optimizing style compiler for React Native and web.
items.useWhen: Use instead of building a shared design-token system and component set separately for React Native and React web.
cautions: The optimizing compiler adds bundler configuration; it is optional.
Large API surface; adopt components incrementally.
install: Install with the project's package manager and commit the lockfile; pin the reviewed version.

items.name: gluestack-ui

license.scope: MIT for the upstream code; check bundled third-party notices.

items.summary: Copy-paste accessible React Native and web components styled with NativeWind/Tailwind.
items.useWhen: Use instead of hand-writing accessible buttons, inputs, modals and menus for a React Native + NativeWind app.
cautions: Components are copied into the project by the CLI; you own updates afterwards.
Older @gluestack-ui/themed packages use a different (ISC) package and API.
install: Install with the project's package manager and commit the lockfile; pin the reviewed version.

items.name: React Native Reanimated

license.scope: MIT for the upstream code; check bundled third-party notices.

items.summary: UI-thread animation library for React Native with shared values, layout animations and worklets.
items.useWhen: Use instead of hand-writing Animated API code that drops frames when the JS thread is busy.
cautions: Versions are tied to React Native architecture; check the compatibility table.
Respect reduced-motion settings for accessibility.
install: Install with the project's package manager and commit the lockfile; pin the reviewed version.

items.name: React Native Gesture Handler

license.scope: MIT for the upstream code; check bundled third-party notices.

items.summary: Native-driven gesture system (pan, pinch, swipe, long-press) for React Native.
items.useWhen: Use instead of hand-writing PanResponder gesture logic and conflict resolution between nested scrollables.
cautions: Wrap the app root in GestureHandlerRootView.
Pair with Reanimated for UI-thread gesture animations.
install: Install with the project's package manager and commit the lockfile; pin the reviewed version.

items.name: react-native-mmkv

license.scope: MIT for the upstream code; check bundled third-party notices.

items.summary: Fast synchronous key-value storage for React Native backed by Tencent MMKV.
items.useWhen: Use instead of AsyncStorage wrappers and hand-written caching for settings, flags and small persisted state.
cautions: Not a secure store for secrets or tokens; use the platform Keychain/Keystore.
Recent majors require the New Architecture.
install: Install with the project's package manager and commit the lockfile; pin the reviewed version.

items.name: FlashList

license.scope: MIT for the upstream code; check bundled third-party notices.

items.summary: High-performance recycling list component for React Native from Shopify.
items.useWhen: Use instead of tuning FlatList windowing by hand for long, heterogeneous feeds.
cautions: v2 targets the New Architecture; v1 APIs (estimatedItemSize) differ.
Keep item components pure to benefit from recycling.
install: Install with the project's package manager and commit the lockfile; pin the reviewed version.

items.name: Flutter

license.scope: BSD-3-Clause for the upstream code; check bundled third-party notices.

items.summary: Google UI toolkit for building natively compiled mobile, desktop and web apps from one Dart codebase.
items.useWhen: Use instead of maintaining separate native UI codebases when pixel-consistent cross-platform UI is the goal.
cautions: Platform-specific features need plugins or platform channels.
Pin the Flutter SDK version (e.g. via FVM or CI config).
install: Install the Flutter SDK from docs.flutter.dev and pin the SDK version in CI.

items.name: Riverpod

license.scope: MIT for the upstream code; check bundled third-party notices.

items.summary: Compile-safe reactive state management and dependency injection for Dart and Flutter.
items.useWhen: Use instead of hand-written InheritedWidget/ChangeNotifier plumbing for app state, caching and async loading.
cautions: Code generation (riverpod_generator) is optional but changes the style; pick one per project.
Major versions changed provider APIs.
install: Add with `flutter pub add flutter_riverpod` and commit pubspec.lock.

items.name: Bloc

license.scope: MIT for the upstream code; check bundled third-party notices.

items.summary: Predictable event-driven state management (Bloc/Cubit) for Dart and Flutter.
items.useWhen: Use instead of ad-hoc setState and stream controllers when business logic needs testable, explicit state transitions.
cautions: More boilerplate than Riverpod for simple state; use Cubit for small cases.
install: Add with `flutter pub add flutter_bloc` and commit pubspec.lock.

items.name: go_router

license.scope: BSD-3-Clause for the upstream code; check bundled third-party notices.

items.summary: Declarative URL-based router for Flutter maintained by the Flutter team.
items.useWhen: Use instead of hand-writing Navigator 2.0 Router delegates, deep links and redirect guards.
cautions: The Flutter team describes it as feature-complete; new routing features may be limited.
Test redirects for auth state changes.
install: Add with `flutter pub add go_router` and commit pubspec.lock.

items.name: dio

license.scope: MIT for the upstream code; check bundled third-party notices.

items.summary: HTTP client for Dart with interceptors, cancellation, form data and timeouts.
items.useWhen: Use instead of hand-writing retry/auth interceptors, multipart uploads and timeout handling on top of package:http.
cautions: Never log full request headers in interceptors; they carry tokens.
install: Add with `flutter pub add dio` (or `dart pub add dio`) and commit pubspec.lock.

items.name: Capacitor

license.scope: MIT for the upstream code; check bundled third-party notices.

items.summary: Native runtime that ships an existing web app to iOS and Android with a plugin API.
items.useWhen: Use instead of rewriting a working web app natively or hand-writing WebView bridges for camera, files and push.
cautions: WebView performance limits heavy animation and long lists.
Commit the generated ios/android projects and keep plugins on the same major.
install: Install with the project's package manager and commit the lockfile; pin the reviewed version.

items.name: Ionic Framework

license.scope: MIT for the upstream code; check bundled third-party notices.

items.summary: Mobile-styled web component library with React, Angular and Vue bindings.
items.useWhen: Use instead of hand-building iOS/Material-styled tabs, sheets and lists for a hybrid (Capacitor) app.
cautions: Adaptive styling looks native-like but is still web UI; test on devices.
install: Install with the project's package manager and commit the lockfile; pin the reviewed version.

items.name: Kotlin Multiplatform

license.scope: Apache-2.0 for the upstream project; this record is a reference.

items.summary: Kotlin technology for sharing business logic (and optionally UI) across Android, iOS, desktop and server.
items.useWhen: Use instead of duplicating networking, persistence and domain logic in Swift and Kotlin while keeping native UIs.
cautions: iOS interop goes through Objective-C headers; check Swift ergonomics.
Pin Kotlin and Gradle plugin versions together.
install: Generate a project with the official KMP wizard and pin Kotlin/Gradle plugin versions.

items.name: Compose Multiplatform

license.scope: Apache-2.0 for the upstream code; check bundled third-party notices.

items.summary: JetBrains declarative UI framework that brings Jetpack Compose to iOS, desktop and web.
items.useWhen: Use instead of writing separate SwiftUI and Compose screens when a Kotlin team wants shared UI.
cautions: iOS and web targets mature at different rates; check stability per target.
install: Apply the org.jetbrains.compose Gradle plugin with a pinned version.

items.name: Jetpack Compose samples

license.scope: Apache-2.0 for the upstream project; this record is a reference.

items.summary: Official Android sample apps demonstrating Jetpack Compose UI patterns.
items.useWhen: Use as a reference instead of inventing Compose architecture, theming and navigation patterns from scratch.
cautions: Samples demonstrate patterns; copy selectively and keep Apache-2.0 notices.
install: Reference only; consult the docs for the version in use.

items.name: SwiftUI documentation

license.scope: Apple developer documentation under Apple terms; reference only, not redistributable code.

items.summary: Apple reference documentation and tutorials for building SwiftUI apps on iOS, macOS and other Apple platforms.
items.useWhen: Use as the authoritative API reference instead of guessing SwiftUI APIs or availability per OS version.
cautions: Check minimum OS availability annotations for each API.
install: Reference only; consult the docs for the version in use.

items.name: fastlane

license.scope: MIT for the upstream code; check bundled third-party notices.

items.summary: Automation tool for building, signing, screenshotting and releasing iOS and Android apps.
items.useWhen: Use instead of hand-written shell scripts for code signing, TestFlight/Play uploads and store metadata.
cautions: Keep App Store Connect API keys and signing material in CI secrets, never in the repo.
Pin the version with a Gemfile/Bundler.
install: Add to a Gemfile, run with `bundle exec fastlane`, and commit Gemfile.lock.

items.name: Electron

license.scope: MIT for the upstream code; check bundled third-party notices.

items.summary: Framework for cross-platform desktop apps with Chromium and Node.js.
items.useWhen: Use instead of separate native desktop codebases when the app is a web UI that needs OS integration.
cautions: Enable contextIsolation and sandbox; never expose Node APIs to remote content.
Large bundle size; ship security updates promptly.
install: Install with the project's package manager and commit the lockfile; pin the reviewed version.

items.name: electron-builder

license.scope: MIT for the upstream code; check bundled third-party notices.

items.summary: Packaging and installer builder for Electron apps (dmg, NSIS, AppImage, snap) with signing support.
items.useWhen: Use instead of hand-scripting installers, code signing and notarization for Electron releases.
cautions: Signing/notarization credentials belong in CI secrets.
Choose either electron-builder or Electron Forge, not both.
install: Install with the project's package manager and commit the lockfile; pin the reviewed version.

items.name: Electron Forge

license.scope: MIT for the upstream code; check bundled third-party notices.

items.summary: Official Electron toolchain for scaffolding, packaging and publishing desktop apps.
items.useWhen: Use instead of assembling bundler, packager and publisher scripts by hand for a new Electron app.
cautions: Plugin/maker versions must match the Forge major.
install: Install with the project's package manager and commit the lockfile; pin the reviewed version.

items.name: electron-updater

license.scope: MIT for the upstream code; check bundled third-party notices.

items.summary: Auto-update module for Electron apps packaged with electron-builder.
items.useWhen: Use instead of hand-writing update download, signature verification and restart logic for Electron.
cautions: Serve updates over HTTPS and keep apps signed so updates verify.
Test update paths from the previous release before shipping.
install: Install with the project's package manager and commit the lockfile; pin the reviewed version.

items.name: Tauri

license.scope: Apache-2.0 OR MIT for the upstream code; check bundled third-party notices.

items.summary: Rust-based framework for small, secure desktop and mobile apps with a web frontend and system WebView.
items.useWhen: Use instead of Electron when bundle size and memory matter, or instead of hand-writing native shells around a web UI.
cautions: UI renders in the OS WebView, so test each platform engine.
Grant capabilities/permissions narrowly in tauri config.
install: Install with the project's package manager and commit the lockfile; pin the reviewed version.

items.name: Tauri plugins workspace

license.scope: Apache-2.0 OR MIT for the upstream code; check bundled third-party notices.

items.summary: Official Tauri plugins for file system, updater, store, notifications, dialogs, shell and more.
items.useWhen: Use instead of hand-writing Rust commands for common OS features like auto-update, dialogs and persisted settings in a Tauri app.
cautions: Each plugin needs explicit capability permissions; grant the minimum.
Keep plugin versions aligned with the Tauri major.
install: Install with the project's package manager and commit the lockfile; pin the reviewed version.

items.name: Wails

license.scope: MIT for the upstream code; check bundled third-party notices.

items.summary: Go framework for desktop apps with a web frontend rendered in the system WebView.
items.useWhen: Use instead of Electron when the backend is Go and you want generated TypeScript bindings to Go methods.
cautions: v3 is in development with a different API; pin v2 or v3 deliberately.
install: Install the wails CLI with a pinned version and commit go.sum.

items.name: Neutralinojs

license.scope: MIT for the upstream code; check bundled third-party notices.

items.summary: Lightweight cross-platform desktop runtime using the OS WebView and a small native binary.
items.useWhen: Use instead of Electron for small utility apps where a tiny download matters and Node APIs are not needed.
cautions: Smaller ecosystem; native extensions run as separate processes.
Restrict the native API allowlist.
install: Install with the project's package manager and commit the lockfile; pin the reviewed version.

items.name: Avalonia UI

license.scope: MIT for the upstream code; check bundled third-party notices.

items.summary: Cross-platform XAML-based .NET UI framework for Windows, macOS, Linux, mobile and WebAssembly.
items.useWhen: Use instead of WPF-only code when a .NET desktop app must also run on macOS and Linux.
cautions: Some add-ons (e.g. Accelerate tooling) are commercial; the core is MIT.
install: Add via `dotnet add package Avalonia` with a pinned version.

items.name: .NET MAUI

license.scope: MIT for the upstream code; check bundled third-party notices.

items.summary: Microsoft cross-platform .NET UI framework for Android, iOS, macOS and Windows.
items.useWhen: Use instead of separate Xamarin/native projects when a C# team targets mobile and Windows/macOS together.
cautions: No official Linux desktop target.
Workload versions are tied to the .NET SDK; pin via global.json.
install: Install with `dotnet workload install maui` and pin the SDK in global.json.

items.name: Slint

license.scope: Triple-licensed: GPLv3, a royalty-free license for desktop/mobile/web apps with attribution conditions, or a paid commercial license (needed for many embedded uses). Review before shipping.

items.summary: Declarative native UI toolkit for Rust, C++, JavaScript and Python apps, including embedded devices.
items.useWhen: Use instead of hand-drawing native widgets when a Rust/C++ app needs a lightweight declarative GUI.
cautions: Confirm which license option applies before distribution.
install: Install with the project's package manager and commit the lockfile; pin the reviewed version.

items.name: egui

license.scope: MIT OR Apache-2.0 for the upstream code; check bundled third-party notices.

items.summary: Immediate-mode GUI library for Rust with the eframe app framework for native and web.
items.useWhen: Use instead of building widget toolkits by hand for Rust tools, debug panels and in-game editors.
cautions: Immediate-mode redraws suit tools more than highly styled consumer apps.
Accessibility support is improving; verify for your use case.
install: Install with the project's package manager and commit the lockfile; pin the reviewed version.

items.name: Iced

license.scope: MIT for the upstream code; check bundled third-party notices.

items.summary: Cross-platform Elm-inspired GUI library for Rust.
items.useWhen: Use instead of hand-written retained-mode UI state handling in a Rust desktop app.
cautions: Pre-1.0: APIs change between minor versions.
install: Install with the project's package manager and commit the lockfile; pin the reviewed version.

items.name: Fyne

license.scope: BSD-3-Clause for the upstream code; check bundled third-party notices.

items.summary: Cross-platform GUI toolkit for Go apps on desktop and mobile.
items.useWhen: Use instead of binding native GUI toolkits by hand when a Go app needs a simple desktop UI.
cautions: Requires CGO and a C toolchain for builds.
Material-inspired look rather than native widgets.
install: Add with `go get fyne.io/fyne/v2@<version>` and commit go.sum.

items.name: Commander.js

license.scope: MIT for the upstream code; check bundled third-party notices.

items.summary: Complete command-line argument parser and subcommand framework for Node.js.
items.useWhen: Use instead of hand-parsing process.argv, help text and subcommands in a Node CLI.
cautions: Major versions change defaults (e.g. option value storage); read the changelog when upgrading.
install: Install with the project's package manager and commit the lockfile; pin the reviewed version.

items.name: yargs

license.scope: MIT for the upstream code; check bundled third-party notices.

items.summary: Node.js argument parser with commands, validation, completion and generated help.
items.useWhen: Use instead of hand-written argv parsing, option validation and shell completion scripts.
cautions: ESM-first in recent majors; check import style.
install: Install with the project's package manager and commit the lockfile; pin the reviewed version.

items.name: oclif

license.scope: MIT for the upstream code; check bundled third-party notices.

items.summary: Framework for building large, plugin-capable TypeScript CLIs (from Salesforce/Heroku).
items.useWhen: Use instead of building command discovery, plugins, help and auto-update plumbing for a multi-command CLI.
cautions: Heavier than Commander for single-command tools.
install: Install with the project's package manager and commit the lockfile; pin the reviewed version.

items.name: Clack prompts

license.scope: MIT for the upstream code; check bundled third-party notices.

items.summary: Styled interactive prompts (text, select, confirm, spinner) for Node CLIs.
items.useWhen: Use instead of hand-writing readline prompt loops and spinners for setup wizards.
cautions: Always provide non-interactive flags for CI; detect TTY before prompting.
install: Install with the project's package manager and commit the lockfile; pin the reviewed version.

items.name: Inquirer.js

license.scope: MIT for the upstream code; check bundled third-party notices.

items.summary: Collection of interactive command-line prompts for Node.js.
items.useWhen: Use instead of hand-writing list, checkbox, password and editor prompts with readline.
cautions: Use the modern @inquirer/prompts package; the legacy inquirer API differs.
Provide flags for non-interactive use.
install: Install with the project's package manager and commit the lockfile; pin the reviewed version.

items.name: Ink

license.scope: MIT for the upstream code; check bundled third-party notices.

items.summary: React renderer for building interactive terminal UIs with components and Flexbox layout.
items.useWhen: Use instead of hand-managing ANSI cursor movement and redraws for rich interactive terminal apps.
cautions: Requires a TTY for interactive features; handle piped output.
install: Install with the project's package manager and commit the lockfile; pin the reviewed version.

items.name: chalk

license.scope: MIT for the upstream code; check bundled third-party notices.

items.summary: Terminal string styling with automatic color-support detection.
items.useWhen: Use instead of hand-writing ANSI escape codes and NO_COLOR/TTY detection.
cautions: ESM-only since v5; use picocolors for the smallest dependency footprint.
install: Install with the project's package manager and commit the lockfile; pin the reviewed version.

items.name: picocolors

license.scope: ISC for the upstream code; check bundled third-party notices.

items.summary: Tiny, fast terminal color formatting library with no dependencies.
items.useWhen: Use instead of hand-written ANSI color helpers when dependency size matters.
cautions: Minimal API: no 256/truecolor helpers.
install: Install with the project's package manager and commit the lockfile; pin the reviewed version.

items.name: ora

license.scope: MIT for the upstream code; check bundled third-party notices.

items.summary: Elegant terminal spinner for long-running Node CLI tasks.
items.useWhen: Use instead of hand-writing spinner frames, cursor hiding and success/failure symbols.
cautions: ESM-only; disable spinners when output is not a TTY.
install: Install with the project's package manager and commit the lockfile; pin the reviewed version.

items.name: cac

license.scope: MIT for the upstream code; check bundled third-party notices.

items.summary: Small, dependency-free framework for building Node.js command-line apps.
items.useWhen: Use instead of hand-written argv parsing when a lightweight alternative to Commander is preferred.
cautions: Smaller feature set than yargs (no built-in completion).
install: Install with the project's package manager and commit the lockfile; pin the reviewed version.

items.name: citty

license.scope: MIT for the upstream code; check bundled third-party notices.

items.summary: Elegant, typed CLI builder from UnJS with lazy subcommands.
items.useWhen: Use instead of hand-written argv parsing and help output in TypeScript CLIs.
cautions: Pre-1.0; pin the version.
install: Install with the project's package manager and commit the lockfile; pin the reviewed version.

items.name: Node.js single executable applications

license.scope: Node.js core is MIT with bundled third-party notices.

items.summary: Official Node.js feature for packaging a bundled script into a single standalone executable.
items.useWhen: Use instead of the archived pkg tool or hand-rolled launchers when shipping a Node CLI as one binary.
cautions: Bundle to a single script first (e.g. with esbuild); native addons need extra handling.
Sign the resulting binary on macOS/Windows.
install: Follow the Node docs for the exact Node version you ship; it is built into Node, no package install.

items.name: Click

license.scope: BSD-3-Clause for the upstream code; check bundled third-party notices.

items.summary: Composable Python package for building command-line interfaces with decorators.
items.useWhen: Use instead of hand-written argparse subcommand trees, prompts and help formatting.
cautions: Test commands with click.testing.CliRunner.
install: Add to pyproject dependencies with a pinned version and commit the lockfile.

items.name: Typer

license.scope: MIT for the upstream code; check bundled third-party notices.

items.summary: Build Python CLIs from type-hinted functions, built on Click.
items.useWhen: Use instead of hand-declaring argparse options when function type hints can define the CLI.
cautions: Pre-1.0; pin the version.
install: Add to pyproject dependencies with a pinned version and commit the lockfile.

items.name: Rich

license.scope: MIT for the upstream code; check bundled third-party notices.

items.summary: Python library for rich terminal output: tables, progress bars, syntax highlighting and tracebacks.
items.useWhen: Use instead of hand-formatting tables, progress bars and colored logs in Python CLIs.
cautions: Respect NO_COLOR and non-TTY output for logs piped to files.
install: Add to pyproject dependencies with a pinned version and commit the lockfile.

items.name: Textual

license.scope: MIT for the upstream code; check bundled third-party notices.

items.summary: Python framework for building full terminal user interfaces with widgets and CSS-like styling.
items.useWhen: Use instead of hand-written curses code for interactive Python terminal apps.
cautions: Async event model; test with the built-in pilot testing API.
install: Add to pyproject dependencies with a pinned version and commit the lockfile.

items.name: questionary

license.scope: MIT for the upstream code; check bundled third-party notices.

items.summary: Python library for interactive command-line prompts (select, checkbox, confirm, text).
items.useWhen: Use instead of hand-written input() loops and menu rendering in Python CLIs.
cautions: Provide flags for non-interactive/CI use.
install: Add to pyproject dependencies with a pinned version and commit the lockfile.

items.name: Cobra

license.scope: Apache-2.0 for the upstream code; check bundled third-party notices.

items.summary: Go library for modern CLI applications with subcommands, flags and shell completion.
items.useWhen: Use instead of hand-wiring the flag package into subcommand trees, help and completion in Go.
cautions: Keep business logic out of command constructors so it stays testable.
install: Add with `go get github.com/spf13/cobra@<version>` and commit go.sum.

items.name: Viper

license.scope: MIT for the upstream code; check bundled third-party notices.

items.summary: Go configuration library merging files, environment variables, flags and defaults.
items.useWhen: Use instead of hand-writing config precedence across YAML/TOML files, env vars and flags in Go.
cautions: Global instance is convenient but hurts testability; prefer viper.New().
Validate config after loading.
install: Add with `go get github.com/spf13/viper@<version>` and commit go.sum.

items.name: Bubble Tea

license.scope: MIT for the upstream code; check bundled third-party notices.

items.summary: Elm-architecture framework for building terminal user interfaces in Go.
items.useWhen: Use instead of hand-managing raw terminal mode, input events and redraws for interactive Go CLIs.
cautions: Pair with Bubbles components and Lip Gloss styling rather than reimplementing them.
install: Add with `go get` at a pinned version and commit go.sum.

items.name: Lip Gloss

license.scope: MIT for the upstream code; check bundled third-party notices.

items.summary: Style definitions for terminal layouts in Go: colors, borders, padding and alignment.
items.useWhen: Use instead of hand-writing ANSI styling and box layout math in Go terminal output.
cautions: Adaptive colors depend on terminal background detection; test light and dark themes.
install: Add with `go get` at a pinned version and commit go.sum.

items.name: urfave/cli

license.scope: MIT for the upstream code; check bundled third-party notices.

items.summary: Declarative, simple package for building command-line apps in Go.
items.useWhen: Use instead of hand-wiring flag parsing and subcommands when Cobra is heavier than needed.
cautions: v3 changes import path and APIs from v2; pick one deliberately.
install: Add with `go get github.com/urfave/cli/v3@<version>` and commit go.sum.

items.name: GoReleaser

license.scope: MIT for the upstream code; check bundled third-party notices.

items.summary: Release automation that cross-compiles, archives, signs and publishes binaries (Go, Rust, Zig and more).
items.useWhen: Use instead of hand-written release scripts for cross-platform builds, checksums, Homebrew taps and GitHub releases.
cautions: GoReleaser Pro features are commercial; the OSS edition is MIT.
Keep signing keys and tokens in CI secrets.
install: Run via the goreleaser/goreleaser-action with a pinned version and a committed .goreleaser.yaml.

items.name: clap

license.scope: MIT OR Apache-2.0 for the upstream code; check bundled third-party notices.

items.summary: Full-featured command-line argument parser for Rust with derive macros.
items.useWhen: Use instead of hand-parsing std::env::args, help text and shell completions in Rust.
cautions: Enable only needed features to limit compile time.
install: Add with `cargo add clap --features derive` and commit Cargo.lock for binaries.

items.name: Ratatui

license.scope: MIT for the upstream code; check bundled third-party notices.

items.summary: Rust library for building rich terminal user interfaces and dashboards.
items.useWhen: Use instead of hand-drawing terminal widgets, layouts and buffers in Rust.
cautions: Restore the terminal on panic; use the provided init/restore helpers.
install: Add with `cargo add ratatui` and commit Cargo.lock for binaries.

items.name: indicatif

license.scope: MIT for the upstream code; check bundled third-party notices.

items.summary: Progress bars and spinners for Rust command-line applications.
items.useWhen: Use instead of hand-writing progress rendering, ETA and multi-bar coordination in Rust CLIs.
cautions: Hide progress output when stderr is not a terminal.
install: Add with `cargo add indicatif` and commit Cargo.lock for binaries.

items.name: dist (cargo-dist)

license.scope: MIT OR Apache-2.0 for the upstream code; check bundled third-party notices.

items.summary: Release tool that builds, packages and publishes Rust (and other) binaries with installers and CI config.
items.useWhen: Use instead of hand-writing GitHub Actions matrices, archives and shell/PowerShell installers for Rust CLI releases.
cautions: Generated CI workflows are regenerated by the tool; avoid hand edits.
install: Install the dist CLI at a pinned version, run `dist init`, and commit the generated config.

items.name: Godot Engine

license.scope: MIT for the upstream code; check bundled third-party notices.

items.summary: Free, open-source 2D and 3D game engine with an integrated editor, GDScript and C#.
items.useWhen: Use instead of writing a custom engine, scene graph, editor and export pipeline for a 2D/3D game.
cautions: Console exports require third-party porting arrangements.
Pin the engine version per project; scenes are not always forward-compatible.
install: Download the pinned editor release from godotengine.org and record the version in the project.

items.name: Phaser

license.scope: MIT for the upstream code; check bundled third-party notices.

items.summary: HTML5 2D game framework for Canvas and WebGL browser games.
items.useWhen: Use instead of hand-writing a game loop, sprite rendering, input, tweens and arcade physics for browser games.
cautions: Major versions (3 vs 4) differ; follow docs for the installed version.
install: Install with the project's package manager and commit the lockfile; pin the reviewed version.

items.name: PixiJS

license.scope: MIT for the upstream code; check bundled third-party notices.

items.summary: Fast 2D WebGL/WebGPU rendering engine for interactive graphics and games.
items.useWhen: Use instead of hand-writing WebGL sprite batching and scene graphs for 2D interactive content.
cautions: Renderer only: add your own physics, audio and game structure.
v8 APIs differ from v7.
install: Install with the project's package manager and commit the lockfile; pin the reviewed version.

items.name: Babylon.js

license.scope: Apache-2.0 for the upstream code; check bundled third-party notices.

items.summary: Full-featured 3D game and rendering engine for the web with WebGL/WebGPU, physics and XR.
items.useWhen: Use instead of assembling a 3D engine (scene, materials, physics, input, XR) by hand for browser games.
cautions: Import from @babylonjs/* modules to tree-shake; the full bundle is large.
install: Install with the project's package manager and commit the lockfile; pin the reviewed version.

items.name: PlayCanvas Engine

license.scope: MIT for the upstream code; check bundled third-party notices.

items.summary: Open-source WebGL/WebGPU 3D game engine; the hosted editor is a separate service.
items.useWhen: Use instead of building a 3D runtime with entity-component structure, physics and asset loading for the web.
cautions: The PlayCanvas cloud editor has paid plans; the engine is MIT.
install: Install with the project's package manager and commit the lockfile; pin the reviewed version.

items.name: Bevy

license.scope: MIT OR Apache-2.0 for the upstream code; check bundled third-party notices.

items.summary: Data-driven ECS game engine written in Rust.
items.useWhen: Use instead of writing a custom ECS, renderer and asset pipeline for a Rust game.
cautions: Pre-1.0: breaking changes every release; follow migration guides.
No visual editor yet.
install: Add with `cargo add bevy` at a pinned version and commit Cargo.lock.

items.name: raylib

license.scope: Zlib for the upstream code; check bundled third-party notices.

items.summary: Simple C library for videogame programming with bindings for many languages.
items.useWhen: Use instead of hand-wiring OpenGL, windowing, input and audio for small games and prototypes.
cautions: Language bindings are community-maintained with varying quality.
install: Use a pinned release or package-manager build (vcpkg, Homebrew) and record the version.

items.name: LÖVE

license.scope: Zlib for the upstream code; check bundled third-party notices.

items.summary: Framework for making 2D games in Lua.
items.useWhen: Use instead of writing windowing, graphics, audio and input layers by hand for a Lua 2D game.
cautions: Bundled libraries carry their own licenses; include notices when distributing.
install: Download a pinned LÖVE release and record the version in the project.

items.name: KAPLAY

license.scope: MIT for the upstream code; check bundled third-party notices.

items.summary: Beginner-friendly JavaScript/TypeScript game library, the maintained fork of Kaboom.js.
items.useWhen: Use instead of hand-writing sprites, collisions and scenes for quick browser games and game jams; use it in place of the unmaintained Kaboom.
cautions: Version numbers jump (3001.x); pin exactly.
install: Install with the project's package manager and commit the lockfile; pin the reviewed version.

items.name: Matter.js

license.scope: MIT for the upstream code; check bundled third-party notices.

items.summary: 2D rigid-body physics engine for the web.
items.useWhen: Use instead of hand-writing collision detection and rigid-body integration for 2D browser games.

items.name: Rapier

license.scope: Apache-2.0 for the upstream code; check bundled third-party notices.

items.name: Excalibur.js

items.useWhen: Use instead of building actors, scenes, collisions and input for a TypeScript browser game by hand.
cautions: Pre-1.0; pin the version.
